description: Functional fail-open vs fail-closed matrix for the AgentISA coordination security layer: scenarios (unregistered resource / unknown data sensitivity / incomplete resource-access policy / normal task, plus a supplementary malformed-registry row) x enforcement modes (strict=False fail-open default vs strict=True fail-closed). Qualitative + counting only: decisions and recorded reasons, no performance quantities.

covered: all four required scenarios x both enforcement modes at the SecurityMonitor.validate_task level (fresh monitor per task x mode)
the supplementary malformed-registry row in both modes
end-to-end propagation through AgentCoordinator.coordinate_task for the same task population (fresh coordinator per task x mode)
violation recording (auditability) for every denial in both modes, and the '(strict mode)' marker on strict denials
not_covered: the always-on authentication/authorization checks are held fixed (all tasks carry tokens); they are not a matrix axis
required_level is LOW everywhere except two normal-task variants (MEDIUM/HIGH); the sensitivity-vs-requirement mismatch path is exercised only by the shipped unit suite, not scaled here
no live network, LLM or ray involvement: posture counting only, so there are no latency/throughput numbers by construction

notes: Qualitative + counting study only: allow/deny decisions and recorded violation reasons. No latency, throughput, memory or any other performance quantity is measured or claimed.
The decision function under test is deterministic; a per-seed stdev of 0.0 reflects that determinism. Seeds vary the task surface (resource names, request shapes, sub-variant mix), not the verdict.

Every task holds the non-varied security dimension at a known-good value (declared data_sensitivity=0 for the resource scenarios; no resources requested for the sensitivity scenarios), so exactly one dimension varies per scenario row.
The same task dict is evaluated in both modes and paired, so mode_divergence is a true per-task 2x2 contingency, not a comparison of independent samples.
Denials are recorded in violation_history in BOTH modes (auditability is not new); what fail-closed adds is the distinguishing reason classes and the '(strict mode)' marker.

The malformed-registry row is supplementary: I4 groups a type-malformed allowed_resources under 'incomplete policy', but its fail-open outcome is a generic deny (a string registry degenerates to a character set), unlike the canonical missing-registry hole which fail-open permits.
